body:
Based on RFC3986, the allowable characters in userinfo are - 
`userinfo    = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" )`

'@' is a gen-delims character and hence disallowed, so I'm guessing this is working as intended?

> Based on RFC3986, the allowable characters in userinfo are -
> `userinfo = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" )`
> 
> '@' is a gen-delims character and hence disallowed, so I'm guessing this is working as intended?

Please note that I am using `HttpUtility.UrlEncode("us@er")`, so the user info part of the URI should be RFC-compliant: in the example code above the URI looks like this: `http://us%40er:password@proxy.acme.com:8080`.
It seems that our URI parser decodes pct-encoded characters before performing any additional operations.
@drfloob Can you please take a look at this?

> I'm trying to connect to my gRPC server through an HTTP proxy. This code works fine until I try using a credentials pair containing the "@" character in the username or in the password

To be clear, does your proxy authentication work when you use credentials that _do not contain_ pct-encoded `@`?

@edoardo-borsato I just want to be sure we're looking at the right symptoms for you. Proxy authentication should work with credentials that do not contain `@`.

That said, there is a problem with gRPC core URI parsing that could be fixed: the userinfo parsing in http_proxy code is performed after the authority has been url-decoded. The URIParser could be improved to parse userinfo from URI authorities before uri-decoding. I'd be happy to review a PR if you want to look into it.

> > I'm trying to connect to my gRPC server through an HTTP proxy. This code works fine until I try using a credentials pair containing the "@" character in the username or in the password
> 
> To be clear, does your proxy authentication work when you use credentials that _do not contain_ pct-encoded `@`?

Hi @drfloob, yes, our proxy authentication works fine when we use credentials with no pct-encoded `@`. We have also tried the following scenarios:
- credentials with no pct-encoded characters at all
- credentials containing some other pct-encoded characters (e.g.: `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`,...)

And in both cases the connection to the gRPC server is correctly established through the proxy.

The bug is right in the proxy setup:

https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70d9ccf576f71c13d3399e7c50fdf37048cac3df/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/http_proxy.cc#L89-L112


1. First the URL is parsed (which decodes pct-encoding).
`url=http://user%40example:password@proxy`
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70d9ccf576f71c13d3399e7c50fdf37048cac3df/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/http_proxy.cc#L89
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70d9ccf576f71c13d3399e7c50fdf37048cac3df/src/core/lib/uri/uri_parser.cc#L234
`url=http://user@example:password@proxy`

2. Then the authority is split on the wrong `@` part of the now percent-decoded URL.
`uri->authority().c_str()=user@example:password@proxy`
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70d9ccf576f71c13d3399e7c50fdf37048cac3df/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/http_proxy.cc#L103
`authority_strs=["user", "example:password", "proxy"]; authority_nstrs=3`

3. Which subsequently gets discarded without further logging
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70d9ccf576f71c13d3399e7c50fdf37048cac3df/src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/http_proxy.cc#L116

#### Workaround
One workaround is to double-encode grpc_proxy and double-decode on the proxy side if you have control over that.
